Would love to give this app a better review except it keeps deleting half my journal entries. I’m writing them by hand with my Apple Pencil and the app keeps deleting half my entries when I finish. I also can’t undo the deletion so it seems like the app isn’t save my entire entry.

reviews.title: Horrible for hand-writers
reviews.text: I opened the app and was excited to see that the organization was easy to navigate and that journal entries can have pictures, locations, health app info, etc. I was very disappointed to find that handwritten entries don’t save properly. I rewrote my entry twice—by the way, these entries were long. How is documenting your life in a journal going to go well if it doesn’t save? I’m so disappointed. Isn’t this supposed to be made by Apple? How did this get past the developers? Anyway, don’t use it if you’re planning to handwrite and don’t want to go through the trouble of screenshotting your writing each time just to paste it in. So inefficient.

reviews.text: It is not useful

reviews.title: Needs MORE
reviews.text:
Firstly, the entire controls of font are frustrating on the iPhone (notes, numbers, and other applications where typing is needed). However, this is by far the WORST to deal with in the journal. You cannot indent bulleted lists, you have to tap multiple menus to select fonts, then you have to redo this for each word/line. How has no one thought to create a header yet? For any of these apps…

The application would be MUCH better if you could save a template. For example, I have many different journals because I want to separate reflection of my emotions during self growth, store progress of self growth, accountability charts, ideas/lists of goals, and end my journaling with Mindfulness and Stoicism by listing 3 achievements each day. 

This could easily be a template to copy/paste, but I am finding I have to type it each time. I could store an entry and physically copy and paste to save time, but it is still annoying having to navigate between old entries and newly created untried. Instead, you could have a template to paste. 

The app isn’t a total bust and I do like a lot of aspects. However, it could be much better, and should be with how many updates we’ve seen since the release of the journal app. 

Also, how does the State of Mind in health and the Journal not sync?

reviews.title: Need to add lines
reviews.text: I’m sure I am not the first person to write this. The idea of having an integrated Apple specific journaling app is amazing. No subscription price for a journaling app is great! But!! This app needs the option to add lines both college and wide rule etc. the option to customize the page or the ability to upload a template like you can in Goodnotes would be amazing. I would actually switch then. I really want to like and use this app but the ability to have lines would be a great feature to add please. Of course I understand that maybe the intention is to type out your journal but the physical act of writing even if on a digital surface is actually better for your mind and mental health than the typing is. So I would love to be able to write digitally like I do with Goodnotes but it is difficult to keep things organized without the guidance of lines. If ever the option to add lines or a template is added this app would be perfect.

reviews.title: Very buggy & counterproductive
reviews.text: I was looking to switch from physical notes to a digital journal, however this app has proved to be a headache. It tends to crash when using the handwriting tool and the keyboard keeps glitching out after typing a single letter in a text box. Also, some inputs just aren’t saved entirely… I have a 2025 iPad Air so hardware shouldn’t be an issue. I think the default font is also ugly and I don’t want to have to change the font for every single text box I input over hundreds of daily entries (maybe pedantic). It has potential to create nice looking pages, but when productivity is key it has wasted my time.

reviews.title: Updated…Buggy mess
reviews.text: Updated……come on Apple, listen to your users. The newest issue is losing most of my entry. It’s happened twice now after deleting the App and giving it another try. Honestly disappointing that Apple doesn’t fix this App. I’ll gladly pay for a different app to avoid ever using this again. It’s going to take an act of a higher power to stop the popups. Read about the frustrations from others on this topic. I don’t know, maybe I have to turn off sync notifications on all 5 of my apple devices before it finally works but I just can’t stop that annoying pop up. Apple just listen for a change. Otherwise this is a good app. Basic if that’s what one wants which is usually the case. Most people don’t really want bloat with all the bells and whistles. After all, people have been journaling for centuries and what is the main thing that entails: writing down their thoughts, that’s all. Too bad I have to deal with a pop up every time I just want to do that.

reviews.title: Apple has work to do
reviews.text:
It’s incredibly disappointing that Apple has chosen not to develop more native apps for platforms like visionOS or watchOS. Considering the canvas visionOS and spatial computing capabilities, this app and the Apple Invites app would have been fantastic on visionOS. I yearn for the ability to write in the air and would love to have that handwriting experience integrated into a journal. Imagine reliving your day in a spatial experience? That holds immense value for me, and I eagerly anticipate the inclusion of Logitech Muse and other spatial accessories in the Journal app. Additionally, the headset offers remarkable journaling capabilities that Apple could leverage.

I also hope to see watchOS integration. It would truly impress me if they had Apple TV integration. While I’m not sure how, if it somehow synced my listening experience on HomePods, that would be a significant improvement.

Yes, using Apple Pencil on iPad is convenient and has its place. However, the innovation of Vision Pro presents an opportunity for apps like the Journal app to offer intelligent and meaningful experiences. These experiences should encourage design and technology to foster creativity and reflection.

reviews.title: Words, but pictures? Not so much
reviews.text: I have kept paper journals for years, but I spend so much time on my iPad, i thought it made sense to journal there too. The app is fairly straightforward to use, but as a person who has used MSWord, PowerPoint, and other apps to generate documents, this one offers less functionality and a LOT more aggravation. Insert a picture, and it squeezes it into a square tile rather than allowing me to format size and aspect ratio. Type some more, add another picture, and BAM! The first picture has gone skating away to some other location. Imagine how aggravating it is when you have 5-10 images and they ALL start skating around. Adjust font size so my aging eyes can read what I’m writing? Good luck trying to find out where that control is. Want to put words in another color, or do anything that a more conventional program (like MSWord) could do, well, good luck, you’ll be annoyed. But if all you want to do is type words into a journal, with no formatting and limited image management functionality, then this will be sufficient to your needs. Very disappointed with the limited utility of the app.

reviews.title: I don’t have a title
reviews.text:
This pain is so un-matched as I was pouring my heart out about something important. Spent about  over 1 hour, after writing so long and at the end felt such relief that I could see all my mixtures of thoughts in words. Was excited to re-read it for correction and clarity, only for me to highlight a word, and it got cut, so I hit the redo arrow and it cleared almost everything I wrote and left the two paragraphs, so virtually about 5 long paragraphs was cleared, it’s indeed so painful but I feel a bit  okay and instead of seething about it I take solace in that I was able to see it even if it was just for a jiffy and it would have been good to have it saved on my phone and come back to re-read it once in a while but I know too better that’s not gonna happen since it’s off the clipboard and something about writing from the heart is that, the moment has to be right to actually capture the true essence of what you are writing about, well till the moment is right, I will write again and will still use the app. The beauty is that, the moment will come again and I will even write more beautifully about it in ways I can’t imagine. Just thought of letting you guys know what just happened, look at me journaling about this again…hahaha 🤣 , I will save this in the same app to remember this early morning.
Happy Sunday

reviews.title: Frustration at one commonly used aspect
reviews.text: An often used feature of mine is the Backspace key.  When I use it, it seems to surround the entire window of text with a red outline, and I am finding it awkward to manoeuvre back to where it needs to be.  Also, when I left the first page I was composing, and then tried to add further text later, I couldn’t seem to find how to get back into the original page.  I can only enter by starting a fresh, new page.  It can only be ‘user error’.  But it isn’t the usual intuitive app that I’ve become used to.  Even this review has now fallen below the text line on my iPads screen and I can’t seem to increase the page site full screen here.  Even trying to select a ‘new line’ on my keyboard is not allowing me to do so.  It continues to write on the same line / paragraph.

reviews.title: Writing feature needs work
reviews.text:
I love that they made this app, but..  The event suggestion features are a nice prototype, but things are often missing and you can’t edit them to be how you want them. 
But the real problem is writing anything. Editing especially. It’s so caught up with rich text editing that it’s forgotten how undo should work, and loses your work in chunks. It’s even more apparent on the desktop app. I have to write somewhere else and paste in. Hoping for improvement, ideally falling back to 20-30+ year old solutions that don’t need fixing.

reviews.title: Primitive and limited
reviews.text:
I made notes of what we were doing each day on a 5 week holiday. I now want to share these notes with my wife who was with me, and our daughter who wasn’t. There does not seem to be any option to send the journal electronically. All I have managed to do is create about 40 separate text files. This is kot am easy way to shrevwith anyone.
The app seems primitive and very limited. I would have been better off using Word. 
Inwill have to copy and paste all 40 files to a Word document then I will delete the Journal app. Apple should be ashamed of this app.

reviews.title: Terrible. DO NOT USE APPLE PENCIL.
reviews.text: I never write reviews. This is my first review ever actually. I got an iPad and Apple Pencil Pro, and I was excited to use this app for journaling. I thought it could replace a traditional journal and would be a great archive for my memories. Instead, it is an unoptimized mess that has absolutely no support for Apple Pencil. My biggest issue is that I spent a good chunk of my time, writing in a journal entry, but for some reason, the app completely DELETES a huge portion of my entry, or deletes it completely. Mind you, with absolutely no way of recovery. This isn’t simply user error. The app just decides to obliterate whatever I wrote down for no apparent reason at all. Sure this app may work better if you type, but what’s the point of having an Apple Pencil if the native journal app doesn’t even support it. There’s not even a lined journal option. It’s just so disappointing cause I know other people have similar experiences but it’s all buried under people who are satisfied typing in their entires. I actually wrote a review a couple weeks ago on here but that happened to get deleted too when it closed out on its own. I’ve been giving it chances again and again, but this morning was my final straw. I wrote the longest most personal entry and it all got deleted with no chance of recovery. I am extremely disappointed with this app. I hope someone else who experienced this as well can find this review knowing that the frustration is a shared experience. All I ask is you think ab

reviews.title: Horrible with Pencil
reviews.text: I have journaled in paper books for most of my life. I enjoy writing by hand. I was excited when Journal came to the iPad because it would integrate with Apple Pencil. I was also very pleased that I could shut off any and every option so that I could keep the journal entries secure to the device they were on. I would never save anything like this in the cloud. However, I found the experience extremely frustrating. When I would move the text up to try to write towards the bottom of the screen the entry would close itself when I placed the edge of my palm on the screen to write. And when I reopened it the entry was smaller and in a border that was movable. I could drag and drop my text around and out of bounds of the border. And then I couldn’t add space to the bottom of the entry to keep writing with my pencil. And MORE IMPORTANTLY, half of what I had written wasn’t there. What is the point of writing down thoughts that you cannot go back and read? Super disappointing. I’ll be going back to my paper books now.

reviews.title: Finally an Apple Journal app!
reviews.text:
Thank you for finally building an Apple Journal app! I have been stumbling around using other apps or Pages for my journals but they are either clumsy to use for journals or require expensive monthly subscriptions. 
I would like to see some improvements to the formatting, like changing the text color, italics, bold, etc. The current version requires clicking away several times just to make adjustments. 
I love that I can create multiple journals for different aspects of my life. Overall very happy with this, thank you devs!
*Update - Thank you for adding the ability to adjust some of the font formatting (colors, bold, etc) still no font size change ability though. I have also stumbled on a bug. When I go through and change the color of  font for some of the words within a paragraph, if you hit the undo button anywhere on the page, everything changes back to the original font color. This is extremely frustrating, as I have gone through and highlighted words in a journal, then tried to undo a spelling mistake or copy / paste mistake, all of the prior color changes revert back to the original font color.

reviews.title: Buggy
reviews.text: Let me start by saying the app is a great idea and I’m a big fan of apple. The concept of this app is great but it’s too buggy. For example when writing with Apple Pencil onto iPad the app decides to not save half of it when clicking done. I have to rewrite half of it or just leave it. I’ve only used it a handful of times and this is one thing guaranteed to happen unfortunately. Hopefully an easily fixable bug but Journal entries take a lot of time and thought to write and I want to be able to look back in future without half of them missing. This was my main worry about moving from pen and paper to digital, things being deleted and bugs causing headache. I want to save paper and have easy digital journals in one place but this is the one thing that cannot happen in a journal app. Sort it out apple
